cds.title: University of San Diego Common Data Set 2025-2026 (PDF, Office of Institutional Research and Effectiveness)

cost.notes: Full-time (12-18 units per semester) costs for 2026-2027 from the CDS G1/G5, confirmed by the Torero Hub 2026-27 table and USD's international applicant page: tuition $64,100 ($32,050 per semester; $2,210 per unit part-time), mandatory fees $1,099, on-campus food and housing $19,200 (housing $13,450 + meal plan $5,750), books and supplies $1,320. The international page publishes a total estimated cost of attendance of $95,232 for 2026-2027, which also includes mandatory health insurance ($4,158 for August 2026-July 2027) and a combined $6,675 for books, travel and personal expenses; that published total is used and other_usd is left empty. (The Torero Hub 'Total' of $88,397 leaves out books, travel and personal costs.) intl_avg_award_usd is the CDS H6 average institutional (non-need-based) award to 63 nonresident undergraduates ($1,209,013 in total).

stats.notes: From the Common Data Set (Fall 2025 entering class): 17,468 applied, 9,359 admitted, 1,300 enrolled. Residency rows (in-state / out-of-state / international, by address) add up to the totals; the enrolled row also has 21 first-years of unknown residency (728 + 505 + 46 + 21 = 1,300). International: 946 applied, 465 admitted, 46 enrolled (the B2 nonresident first-year count is also 46). The CDS gives no waiting-list, early decision or early action counts. USD is test-free (it does not look at SAT/ACT scores), so C9 lists no score submission or percentiles and no SAT/ACT ranges are shown. The GPA breakdown is the only populated column of C11 (the one headed 'students who submitted scores'; the other two columns are blank), so it is treated as all enrolled first-years; the CDS average of 4.02 is above 4.0, so it is a weighted GPA (USD recalculates a weighted GPA from the transcript), and all of 4.0 and above falls in the top bin. 100% of first-years reported a GPA. Undergraduate enrollment (6,049) and the nonresident count (379) are the B1/B2 'Total Undergraduates' figures. Admit rate by these counts is about 54%.

cds_test_policy.notes: From CDS C8A: USD answers No to using SAT or ACT scores in admission decisions (C7: 'not considered').
